children: By Sudeshna Ghoshal

European shares climbed on Thursday, with risk sentiment boosted by lower oil prices and a pause in the global bond selloff after the U.S. Federal Reserve delivered a widely anticipated interest rate hike.
The pan-European STOXX 600
rose 0.5% to 640.21 points by 0830 GMT, with most regional bourses following suit. Germany's DAX
also climbed 0.5%.
Travel stocks (.SXTP) were among the top gainers, up 0.8%, tracking a retreat in oil prices, with airline stocks Ryanair
and Lufthansa
up 1.1% and 1.2%, respectively.
Automakers (.SXAP) climbed 0.8%, with shares of BMW
, Renault
and Volkswagen
rising around 1% each.
Crude prices extended losses for a second session following reports of Saudi Arabia offering extra crude cargoes through Oman, but Brent crude futures
stayed above $100.
Europe's energy sector (.SXEP) advanced 0.4%, bucking the drop in crude prices.

"Investors are taking some comfort from slightly lower crude prices. They're looking at the prospect of the Bank of England keeping rates on hold later today," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.
The Bank of England is widely expected to leave rates unchanged later in the day, with investors focused on any signals about further policy tightening.
Last week, the European Central Bank raised interest rates for a second time this year.
UK's blue-chip FTSE 100
CURRENCYCOM:UK100
climbed 0.6%, underpinned by banks including HSBC
and healthcare stocks such as AstraZeneca
A final reading of euro zone showed inflation rose to an annual rate of 3.2% in August, revised lower from a preliminary reading of a 3.3% rate.
Meanwhile, long-dated Treasury yields remained below the 5% mark after the U.S. Fed raised interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point, as widely expected, in its first hike since 2023.
"Investors took some comfort from the Fed standing firm in the face of Donald Trump's noisy demands for lower rates and so it adds to the credibility of the Fed," Wealth Club's Streeter said.
Among other individual stocks, Berentzen
jumped 19.4% after the German spirits manufacturer confirmed its negotiations regarding a potential takeover bid from New Orleans-based alcohol producer Sazerac.
Shares of Sodexo
gained 4.4% after JP Morgan upgraded the French caterer's stock rating to "overweight" from "neutral".
Bilfinger
posted its biggest intraday percentage drop on record, down 19.5%, after the German industrial services group lowered its 2026 outlook for the second time.
Raiffeisen Bank International
fell 8.1% after Grizzly Research disclosed a short position on the Austrian lender.
